summary: CURSMGR is a shared DB2 Cursor Manager for online programs. Called with a cursor request, it dispatches on a request type to Declare (D), Open (O), Fetch (F), or Close (C) a cursor, with optional array-fetch for performance, returning a response code. It is the cursor engine INQHIST uses to run its history query. IMPORTANT: the source appears TRUNCATED/INCOMPLETE — only the Declare and Open paragraphs have bodies; the Fetch (P300) and Close (P400) paragraphs are referenced by the dispatcher but their bodies are missing from the source. Since INQHIST issues F (fetch) and C (close) requests, this is a cross-program gap worth SME review.

paragraphs.name: MAINLINE
paragraphs.pseudocode:
SELECT CASE request type
  WHEN 'D': CALL P100-DECLARE-CURSOR
  WHEN 'O': CALL P200-OPEN-CURSOR
  WHEN 'F': CALL P300-FETCH-DATA
  WHEN 'C': CALL P400-CLOSE-CURSOR
END SELECT
CICS RETURN TO caller

annotations.note: SME REVIEW: P300-FETCH-DATA and P400-CLOSE-CURSOR are dispatched here but their paragraph bodies are absent from the source (file appears truncated after P200). Fetch/Close requests would fall through with no action.

paragraphs.name: P100-DECLARE-CURSOR
paragraphs.pseudocode:
SET CURS-RESPONSE-CODE = 0
IF array-fetch requested THEN SET array size = 20 (max) ELSE SET array size = 1 END IF
SQL DECLARE :CURS-NAME CURSOR FOR :CURS-STMT
IF SQLCODE <> 0 THEN SET CURS-RESPONSE-CODE = SQLCODE END IF

annotations.note: Dynamic cursor: DECLARE ... FOR a runtime statement string (:CURS-STMT), so any SQL text the caller supplies can be run.

paragraphs.name: P200-OPEN-CURSOR
paragraphs.pseudocode:
RESET WS-FETCH-COUNT = 0 and WS-ROWS-FETCHED = 0
SQL OPEN :CURS-NAME
IF SQLCODE = 0 THEN SET CURS-RESPONSE-CODE = 0 ELSE SET CURS-RESPONSE-CODE = SQLCODE END IF
branches: IF OPEN SQLCODE=0 -> ok else return sqlcode

annotations.note: Source file ends here — P300-FETCH-DATA / P400-CLOSE-CURSOR (and array-fetch loop) are not present. Incomplete member.
